title: .a11y-local.json
description: Repository configuration for si-a11y, the local WCAG 2.2 A/AA engine. Every field is optional: a missing field takes the default stated here, and a field that does not match this schema is reported and read as its advisory default while the other fields still apply; a file that is not valid JSON, or is empty, applies nothing at all and is reported with the line and column where it stops being JSON, the built-in defaults standing in until it is fixed, so a typo never blocks everything and never ignores everything. Resolution: the engine resolves this file from the ABSOLUTE path of each checked file, taking the nearest .a11y-local.json in the file's own directory or any directory above it, whatever the working directory of the editor, hook or server; a relative file path is refused and reported, never resolved. Commit it at the repository root and it applies to every team member who checks a file in that repository. Without one, the built-in defaults apply: mode "advisory", nothing enforced. A .a11y-local.json that is a symlink pointing outside its own directory is not read; the refusal is reported and the walk continues upward.

$schema.description: Editor hint pointing at this schema. Not read by si-a11y.

mode.description: Which mode applies to every file at or below this file. "advisory", the default (also when the key is missing), reports findings and never fails: no finding blocks and the CLI exits 0. "block" marks each failed finding on a criterion listed in "enforce" as blocking: true, and likewise on a criterion or rule that "levels" puts at "block"; summary.blocking counts those findings, the CLI and the save hooks exit non-zero, and the tools' enforcement block tells the agent it is a stop order. Findings that need human review never block. Any other value is reported and read as "advisory". Every result checked with a file path states the mode that applied and this file's path as enforcement.source. The one permitted local override of this field is the environment variable SI_A11Y_MODE, set to "advisory" or "block" on the developer's machine: its mode then applies in place of this field, and every result reports the override (enforcement.overridden names the project's mode, the effective mode, the variable and its value; the mode: line under the CLI's and both save hooks' summaries names it too), so a gate switched off locally is never switched off in silence. Any other value, an empty string included, is reported as a config_invalid warning and ignored, this field applying. No user-level file changes the mode.

enforce.description: WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA success criteria that block in "block" mode; in "advisory" mode the list has no effect. Default: none. Empty by design: a team opts in criterion by criterion as it cleans up, and lists all 55 for a project that should start clean. An id that is not a WCAG 2.2 A/AA criterion is reported and not enforced; the rest still are. A duplicate id is read once. Shorthand for "levels": listing an id here is the same as giving it the level "block" there, and an explicit "levels" entry for the same id wins (the disagreement is reported as a config_invalid warning).

enumDescriptions: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (Level A)
Content on Hover or Focus (Level AA)
Three Flashes or Below Threshold (Level A)

levels.description: A level per criterion or per rule, so a team tightens gradually: {"1.4.3": "block", "4.1.2": "warn", "sia-r69": "off"}. Keys are WCAG 2.2 Level A and AA criterion ids ("1.4.3") or engine rule ids ("sia-r69", "si-label-02"), the same ids a .a11yignore criterion entry may name; the engine checks each key against its own rule and criterion tables at run time, so this schema can only check the shape. Values: "block" marks each failed finding on the id as blocking: true in "block" mode, exactly as listing a criterion in "enforce" does, and has no effect beyond the default in "advisory" mode; "warn", the default for every id not listed, reports failed findings (in findings and summary.failed) and never blocks, and a finding under an explicit "warn" carries enforcementLevel: "warn" so a reader can tell it from a default-level failure; "off" removes the id's findings from findings and the counts in every mode, as a .a11yignore criterion entry does, and the result's ignored block lists the entry (kind "level", this file as source, no line, reason levels."<id>": "off"). A rule id matches the findings that rule produced (engines.<engine>.rule) and is more specific than its criterion: {"1.1.1": "block", "sia-r2": "warn"} blocks every 1.1.1 failure except the ones sia-r2 found. Precedence over "enforce": an explicit level here wins for the same id, and the disagreement is reported as a config_invalid warning so a reviewer sees that an id in "enforce" does not block; the result's enforcement block counts the ids at "block" from both fields (enforcedCriteria) and lists what applied (levels). An unknown key, or a value outside the three, is reported by name and that entry is read as the default while the other entries still apply. An "off" level on an id that "enforce" lists narrows the gate the way a .a11yignore entry does, and the enforcement instruction says so.

enumDescriptions: A failed finding is a stop order in block mode (blocking: true); no effect beyond the default in advisory mode.
The default: a failed finding is reported and never blocks; written explicitly, it marks the finding enforcementLevel: "warn".
The id's findings are not reported in findings or the counts, in every mode; the ignored block lists the entry.

ignore.description: Paths si-a11y must not assess, in .gitignore syntax: the same engine as .a11yignore. `*` stands for anything but a slash, `**` spans directories, a pattern with no slash matches by name at any depth, a leading `/` anchors to this file's folder, a trailing `/` means a directory, `!` puts a path back and `re:` takes a regular expression. Patterns are matched relative to this file's folder, and nothing may follow a pattern in its string (a trailing # comment is read as part of the pattern). Every skip is reported, so an exclusion can never look like a clean result: the skip's excludedBy names the rule and this file as source. Setting this replaces the default list, so repeat the defaults you want to keep. This list is path-only and carries no reasons (the skip then has no reason key); a criterion to suppress, and a reason per entry, belong in .a11yignore.

telemetry.description: Anonymous usage statistics (counts and codes only; see PRIVACY.md). "off" opts this repository out. Accepts "on"/"off", true/false, or an object with "enabled".
